method: Read current local adapter, model catalog and billing guard; inspect current Anthropic official documentation and compare each contract. Run one in-memory synthetic usage guard counterexample. No credentials, env files, authenticated API calls, inference POSTs, paid calls, price changes or product source changes.

model.access: public official documentation opened successfully; no account API queried
model.documented: Claude API model ID claude-haiku-5-5, active, released 2026-10-07, context window 1M, max output 128K; text/images to text and documented tool support.
model.local: model_selection.py:9–10 and chat_models.py:8 use the same ID but label integration and revision pinning unverified; general limits at chat_general.py:25–28 are 4096 input and 4096 output, not the provider maximum.
model.versioning: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/model-ids-and-versions states 4.6-and-later dateless IDs identify a fixed model snapshot, while serving infrastructure can change. This is documentation evidence; no live response or account-specific model/capability receipt is available.
model.account_limit: Official listing is not proof of account entitlement, connected key/workspace, regional access, network behavior, or real deployment. If an ID becomes unconfirmed or unavailable, refuse execution rather than silently substituting a different model. Models API availability/capability checks require separately authorized authenticated use.

transport.documented: Messages POST /v1/messages; count POST /v1/messages/count_tokens; documented count returns input_tokens and can include system/messages/tools, thinking and output_config. Required API version header is documented; official examples use 2023-06-01 and x-api-key. GET /v1/models provides available model IDs and capabilities.
transport.local: anthropic_ontology.py:13–15,161–202,256–257 pins first-party endpoints, 2023-06-01, JSON, x-api-key, bounded payload, no retry or redirect. chat_runtime.py:79–104 injects credentials. chat_general.py:321–361 builds separately hashed count/message payloads; non-test actual transport is disabled in chat_general.py:131–138 and 475–478.
transport.limitations: Documentation compatibility is not a successful real HTTP request, response schema validation, account access, cost reconciliation, or user workflow. The locally named credential supplier is not evidence that credentials exist. A documentation GET page is not an API GET.

thinking_and_tools.documented: Haiku 5.5 accepts disabled thinking at low, medium, or high effort; effort must not change in the same conversation while thinking is disabled. Client tools are executed by the application and require tool_result continuation; server tools have separate provider execution and possible charges.
thinking_and_tools.local: chat_models.py:63–67 uses low effort; live-style preview adds disabled thinking at chat_general.py:328–335; tools are restricted to named client tools at chat_general.py:32–34 and strict schemas are generated. Current documentation supports this model-specific combination, but strict tool schema and actual end-to-end behavior remain unverified against the account.
thinking_and_tools.recommendation: Keep tool definitions, settings, count body, message body, exact consent and output restrictions bound to the request; validate actual model-specific capabilities rather than extrapolating disabled thinking to another model. No automatic fallback or model change.

pricing.documented_usd_per_million_tokens: For Haiku 5.5 prompt length <=100000: input 0.10, output 0.50; >100000: input 0.50, output 2.50. The threshold includes cache writes and reads. Price table separately lists cache writes/hits; US-only inference is a 1.1 multiplier for 4.6+; client tools use normal token prices; server tools can incur additional charges.
pricing.local: chat_models.py:8,84–95 matches documented standard no-cache text rate and uses >100000 cutoff; the present general 4096 input ceiling does not itself establish all hidden billable dimensions. Nonzero cache and unsupported dimensions are deliberately not priced.
pricing.tiers_and_speed: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/api/service-tiers says auto is default and standard_only is available; current page excludes Haiku 5.5 from Priority Tier. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing lists fast mode for specified Opus models, not Haiku 5.5. The request currently omits explicit tier/speed; do not generalize this model-specific availability to other models.
pricing.count_limit: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/token-counting describes token counting as an estimate and says counting does not apply prompt caching. Count is not an invoice, paid usage proof, or guaranteed final billed total.
pricing.policy: No rate, budget, ledger, or automatic billing policy changed. A changed pricing policy needs documented cost bounds, user-visible consent and the appropriate approval before activation.

usage_guard_feasibility.local: chat_models.py:125–157 requires usage.service_tier, speed, inference_geo and server_tool_use and valid zero cache counters when require_billing_evidence is true. server_tool_use must be exactly the two keys web_fetch_requests and web_search_requests with integer zeros.
usage_guard_feasibility.direct_synthetic_result: In-memory response with model claude-haiku-5-5, input 100, output 50, zero cache counters, standard tier/speed and global region but no server_tool_use returned insufficient_billing_evidence. Adding server_tool_use={web_fetch_requests:0,web_search_requests:0} returned no unpriced reason. No real provider response was used.
usage_guard_feasibility.documentation_evidence: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/handling-stop-reasons has a concise successful-response example showing only input/output usage. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing illustrates separate server_tool_use objects containing only web_search_requests, only web_fetch_requests, or code_execution_requests. The full Messages reference shows a richer object, but examples are illustrative and do not establish which fields are guaranteed on each real request or response/version.
usage_guard_feasibility.interpretation: The current strict policy can conservatively leave a response unpriced if expected dimensions are absent or differently shaped; do not call this a provider error or claim its frequency is known. It intentionally prevents underpricing and must not be weakened by treating unknown, null, nonzero, or unrecognized usage as zero. Absence from a documentation example does not prove actual omission or a normative schema rule.
usage_guard_feasibility.safe_design_question: Before enabling real traffic, define and verify exact server-controlled request features, a model/price/version policy, provider response evidence, alternative bounded evidence if a supported optional field is omitted, and unknown-cost reconciliation. Only use an absence as proof of zero where an applicable official contract and the bound request explicitly establish that inference; otherwise retain uncertainty. Validate with authorized, bounded real account receipts separately.

overall: Official documentation confirms the selected model ID and rates and supports the documented basic request shape, but account availability, live payload behavior, actual provider usage shapes, end-to-end operation, and real billing reconciliation remain unverified. Current general live runtime explicitly refuses non-test transport. This review does not authorize enabling it or performing a paid test.
